blocks.heading: General period
blocks.text: The general limitation period for ordinary synthetic civil claims is three years from the date the claimant knew about the violation.

blocks.heading: Warranty period
blocks.text: The special warranty limitation period is one year for synthetic warranty claims.

blocks.heading: Employment period
blocks.text: The employment claim limitation period is six months in this synthetic policy.

blocks.heading: Exception
blocks.text: A special statute may override the general limitation period when an explicit exception exists.

blocks.heading: Notice
blocks.text: A claimant should preserve written notice evidence before the limitation period expires.

blocks.heading: General notice
blocks.text: A standard synthetic service contract may be terminated with thirty days written notice.

blocks.heading: Breach notice
blocks.text: Termination for material breach requires ten days cure notice before termination.

blocks.heading: Immediate termination
blocks.text: Immediate termination is allowed only for fraud, sanctions, or severe data misuse.

blocks.heading: Notice format
blocks.text: Termination notice must identify the contract, effective date, and authorized signer.

blocks.heading: Forbidden shortcut
blocks.text: Oral termination is not sufficient under this synthetic rule set.

blocks.heading: Scope
blocks.text: Confidential information includes business secrets, customer data, incident evidence and unreleased technical designs.

blocks.heading: Duration
blocks.text: The confidentiality obligation survives for five years after contract termination.

blocks.heading: Exception
blocks.text: Information already public without breach is not treated as confidential.

blocks.heading: Incident evidence
blocks.text: Incident response evidence must be shared only with authorized internal reviewers.

blocks.heading: Return
blocks.text: At termination the receiving party must return or destroy confidential materials.

title: Synthetic document retention and legal hold

blocks.heading: Standard retention
blocks.text: Routine synthetic audit evidence is retained for seven years.

blocks.heading: Short retention
blocks.text: Temporary processing logs are retained for ninety days unless a legal hold is applied.

blocks.heading: Legal hold
blocks.text: A legal hold suspends ordinary deletion and retention purge until the hold is released.

blocks.heading: Owner
blocks.text: The compliance owner records the reason, start date and release date for each hold.

blocks.heading: Conflict
blocks.text: When retention expiry conflicts with legal hold, legal hold has priority.

blocks.heading: Trigger
blocks.text: A force majeure event must be external, unavoidable and directly prevent performance.

blocks.heading: Notice
blocks.text: The affected party must send force majeure notice within five business days.

blocks.heading: Payment exception
blocks.text: Payment obligations are not automatically suspended by force majeure in this synthetic rule.

blocks.heading: Mitigation
blocks.text: The affected party must use reasonable mitigation measures.

blocks.heading: End
blocks.text: Performance resumes when the force majeure event no longer prevents performance.

blocks.heading: Consent
blocks.text: Synthetic personal data processing requires explicit consent unless another lawful basis applies.

blocks.heading: Withdrawal
blocks.text: Consent may be withdrawn at any time through the designated request channel.

blocks.heading: Audit
blocks.text: Consent records must include timestamp, source system and consent text version.

blocks.heading: Minors
blocks.text: Processing data of minors requires additional guardian approval in this synthetic policy.

blocks.heading: Forbidden assumption
blocks.text: Silence is not treated as consent.

blocks.heading: Chain of custody
blocks.text: Audit evidence must preserve chain of custody, collector identity and timestamp.

blocks.heading: Restricted access
blocks.text: Restricted audit evidence is visible only to restricted callers.

blocks.heading: Redaction
blocks.text: Personal data should be redacted before external disclosure unless disclosure is legally required.

blocks.heading: Integrity
blocks.text: Hash verification is required before audit evidence is accepted into a report.

blocks.heading: Retention
blocks.text: Critical audit evidence is retained for ten years under the synthetic rule set.
